full_judgment:
This appeal, by defendant No. 1, has arisen out of a judgment and final decree passed in a suit for declaration of title and for partition. 

 2. In the preliminary decree the trial court decreed that the plaintiff would get 19th/288 share in the suit land. On 23.2.72 the plaintiff filed an application for partition through ah Advocate Commissioner. The plaintiff's prayer was allowed and a writ was issued appointing Mr. A. Rashid as Commissioner by order No 78 dated 9.3.72. From 31.3.72 to 13.1.73, Order Nos. 79 to 86 "the Court awaited for the commissioner's report". On 13 1.73 the order was, "To 19.3.74 for awaiting Commissioner's report & order", No order was passed on 19.3.73. On 20.3.73 the pleader commissioner submitted his report and the parties were directed to make note of it and file an objection, if any, by 21.4 73. By 21.4.73 parties did not file any objection against the report and it was ordered "put up on 22.5.73 for order and for objection, if any". On 22.5.73 no objection was filed and the Court accepted the report of the Commissioner and ordered that the suit be decreed finally and the preliminary decree dated 6.6.70 he made final and the Commissioner's report, map, field book and Chitta be made part of the decree. 

 3. On behalf of the appellant it has been contended that the learned Advocate for the defendant appellant was not served with a copy of the application for appointment of commissioner, and the order dated 20.3 73 was not shown to him, hence the appellant was deprived of all opportunities to file an objection to the report of the Commissioner, and that the acceptance of such report in passing the final decree and making it a part of it was not done lawfully. In support of this contention reliance has been placed on Muhammad Ramjan Vs. Fazlul Huq reported in (1963) 15 DLR 99 = P.L.D. 1963 Dacca 987. 

 4. On the other hand it has been contended by respondent that the appellant had never been prejudiced as he was present when the commissioner went to the locality and it was the duty of the learned Advocate of the defendant to keep himself abreast with the subsequent orders of the Court. It has been urged that in order to delay the matter the defendant did not make any objection though more than one opportunity was given to him by the Court. It has further been submitted that report of the Commissioner cannot be challenged in second appeal when it had already got merged in the final decree. On behalf of the respondent reliance has been placed on Kristian Reddiar V. Ramanuja Reddiar reported In A.I.R. 1929 M d. 492. In this case it was observed: 

 6. In the case reported in (I 963) 15 DLR 99= PLD 1963 Dac 987 an order was passed by the executing court directing the decree-holder to take further steps, but the order was not shown to the learned Advocate concerned. In that case a reference was made to Rule 466 

 9. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court confirming the final decree of the trial Court set aside. The matter is sent back to the trial Court for giving an opportunity to the defendant to file an objection. The trial Court is directed to dispense of the matter expeditiously.
